keywords.def: a historical period of cultural, artistic, and scientific revival in Europe
born to parents who are not married
a system of learning a skill by working with an expert
financial support given to artists or thinkers
an artist’s greatest or most important work
the arrangement of elements in a piece of art
the study of the structure of the human body

sentences.en: Leonardo Da Vinci was one of the greatest minds in history.
sentences.zh: 列奥纳多·达·芬奇是历史上最伟大的智者之一。

sentences.en: He painted some of the most famous works of art ever: the Mona Lisa, Last Supper, and more.
sentences.zh: 他创作了一些史上最著名的艺术作品：蒙娜丽莎、最后的晚餐等等。

sentences.en: He was also a scientist, an engineer, an anatomist, and an inventor.
sentences.zh: 他同时也是一位科学家、工程师、解剖学家和发明家。

sentences.en: He is often described as the perfect example of a “Renaissance man.” A Renaissance man is someone who is skilled in many different areas, especially during the time of the Renaissance.
sentences.zh: 人们经常把他描述为“文艺复兴人”的完美典范。文艺复兴人是指在许多不同领域都很精通的人，尤其是在文艺复兴时期。

sentences.en: In today’s episode, we’re going to explore the life of Leonardo da Vinci.
sentences.zh: 在今天的节目中，我们将探讨列奥纳多·达·芬奇的一生。

sentences.en: Who exactly was he? What were his greatest achievements?
sentences.zh: 他究竟是谁？他最伟大的成就是什么？

sentences.en: Can we really call him a scientist? And does his legacy still matter today, more than 500 years after his death?
sentences.zh: 我们真的能称他为科学家吗？在他逝世五百多年后的今天，他的遗产是否依然重要？

sentences.en: And we’ll do this while practicing our English listening comprehension and learning some new vocabulary!
sentences.zh: 我们将在练习英语听力理解和学习一些新词汇的同时完成这一切！

sentences.en: Leonardo da Vinci was born in 1452 in the small Italian town of Vinci.
sentences.zh: 列奥纳多·达·芬奇于1452年出生于意大利小镇芬奇。

sentences.en: His name “da Vinci” is not a modern surname.
sentences.zh: 他的名字“da Vinci”并不是一个现代意义上的姓氏。

sentences.en: It means “Leonardo from the town of Vinci “.
sentences.zh: 它的意思是“来自芬奇镇的列奥纳多”。

sentences.en: Leonardo was an illegitimate child. Illegitimate, in this context, means that he was born to parents who were not married.
sentences.zh: 列奥纳多是一个私生子。在这个语境下，“私生子”意味着他出生时父母并未结婚。

sentences.en: In 15th century Italy, this could limit your opportunities.
sentences.zh: 在15世纪的意大利，这会限制你的发展机会。

sentences.en: It could be challenging, for example, for illegitimate children to go to school.
sentences.zh: 例如，私生子想要上学可能面临很大挑战。

sentences.en: Fortunately for Leonardo, his father treated him well and made sure that he received some education.
sentences.zh: 对于列奥纳多来说幸运的是，他的父亲对很好，并确保他接受了一些教育。

sentences.en: But because he was illegitimate, he was not really able to attend Latin schools.
sentences.zh: 但由于他是私生子，他实际上无法进入拉丁语学校。

sentences.en: Latin, at the time, was a very important language in law and religion and academics.
sentences.zh: 在当时，拉丁语是法律、宗教和学术领域非常重要的语言。

sentences.en: And he was also not able to join his father’s profession.
sentences.zh: 而且他也无法继承他父亲的职业。

sentences.en: So as a teenager, he was sent to the city of Florence, which was one of the most important places during the Renaissance.
sentences.zh: 因此，在十几岁时，他被送到了佛罗伦萨市，那是文艺复兴时期最重要的城市之一。

sentences.en: In Florence, he began an apprenticeship under the artist Andrea del Verrochio Now there’s gonna be a lot of Italian words in this episode.
sentences.zh: 在佛罗伦萨，他在艺术家安德烈·德尔·韦罗基奥的门下开始学艺。这期节目里会有很多意大利语单词。

sentences.en: I don’t speak Italian, so if I make pronunciation mistakes, I am very sorry.
sentences.zh: 我不会说意大利语，所以如果我发音有误，我深表歉意。

sentences.en: But Verrocchio was a master painter, a sculptor, and a goldsmith.
sentences.zh: 但韦罗基奥是一位绘画大师、雕塑家兼金匠。

sentences.en: He was basically a great artist. He worked with all different types of materials.
sentences.zh: 他基本上是一位伟大的艺术家，能使用各种不同的材料进行创作。

sentences.en: An apprenticeship is a system where a young person learns a skill by working closely with an expert.
sentences.zh: 学徒制是一种年轻人通过与专家紧密合作来学习技能的制度。

sentences.en: We still have the idea of apprentices in the UK today.
sentences.zh: 今天在英国，我们仍然保留着学徒的概念。

sentences.en: Maybe in other countries too. People learn vocational or practical skills like construction or plumbing or hairdressing through apprenticeships in the UK.
sentences.zh: 也许其他国家也有。在英国，人们通过学徒制学习建筑、管道工或美发等职业或实用技能。

sentences.en: In Verrocchio’s workshop (a workshop being the place where art and crafts are created), Leonardo studied various different things.
sentences.zh: 在韦罗基奥的工作室（工作室是创作艺术和工艺品的地方），列奥纳多学习了各种不同的东西。

sentences.en: He learned painting, drawing, sculpture, mechanics, and basic engineering.
sentences.zh: 他学习了绘画、素描、雕塑、机械学和基础工程学。

sentences.en: Renaissance artist workshops were very busy environments.
sentences.zh: 文艺复兴时期的艺术家工作室是非常忙碌的环境。

sentences.en: The assistants helped to complete the main artist’s projects, especially their larger projects.
sentences.zh: 助手们协助完成主艺术家的项目，尤其是他们的大型项目。

sentences.en: So working as an apprentice to a master artist gave Leonardo the practical skills that he needed to become a great artist,and also the exposure to a wide range of types of art and disciplines and ways of expressing emotion and being an artist basically.
sentences.zh: 因此，作为艺术大师的学徒，列奥纳多不仅获得了成为伟大艺术家所需的实用技能，还广泛接触了各种艺术、学科以及表达情感和作为艺术家的基本方式。

sentences.en: As I mentioned in the introduction, Leonardo da Vinci has been described as the perfect example of a Renaissance man, so we should probably talk about the Renaissance.
sentences.zh: 正如我在引言中提到的，列奥纳多·达·芬奇一直被描述为文艺复兴人的完美典范，所以我们可能应该谈谈文艺复兴。

sentences.en: The Renaissance was a time of cultural and intellectual change in Europe.
sentences.zh: 文艺复兴是欧洲文化和思想变革的时期。

sentences.en: The word comes from French and means rebirth.
sentences.zh: 这个词来自法语，意思是重生。

sentences.en: The Renaissance was a period of renewed interest in art, literature and knowledge of ancient civilizations like ancient Greece and Ancient Rome.
sentences.zh: 文艺复兴时期人们重新燃起了对艺术、文学以及古希腊和古罗马等古代文明知识的兴趣。

sentences.en: It began in Italy, around the 14th century, and gradually spread across Europe over the next few hundred years.
sentences.zh: 它大约在14世纪起源于意大利，并在随后的几百年里逐渐传遍整个欧洲。

sentences.en: Cities like Florence became places for creativity and innovation.
sentences.zh: 像佛罗伦萨这样的城市成为了充满创造力和创新精神的地方。

sentences.en: One reason for this was wealth. Powerful and rich families like the Medici family used their money to support artists, scientists and thinkers.
sentences.zh: 造成这种情况的一个原因是财富。像美第奇家族这样权势富有的家族用他们的钱来支持艺术家、科学家和思想家。

sentences.en: This kind of support is known as patronage.
sentences.zh: 这种支持被称为赞助。

sentences.en: Patronage refers to financial support given to artists or scholars.
sentences.zh: 赞助是指给予艺术家或学者的资金支持。

sentences.en: On a slight tangent, this system of patronage is still around today.
sentences.zh: 稍微扯远一点，这种赞助制度今天仍然存在。

sentences.en: It is one of the main ways that content creators, like me, make a living.
sentences.zh: 这是像我这样的内容创作者谋生的主要方式之一。

sentences.en: I have a community on a website called “Patreon” where you can become a “patron”.
sentences.zh: 我在一个叫做“Patreon”的网站上有一个社区，你可以在那里成为一名“赞助人”。

sentences.en: Both of these come from the word “patronage”.
sentences.zh: 这两个词都源于“赞助”一词。

sentences.en: So, you can give a small amount of money to support Thinking in English and in return I can make more content and episodes and organize more events.
sentences.zh: 所以，你可以提供少量的资金来支持Thinking in English，作为回报，我可以制作更多内容和节目，并组织更多活动。

sentences.en: So, what made the Renaissance different from before?
sentences.zh: 那么，是什么让文艺复兴与以往不同呢？

sentences.en: There was a focus on humanism. This was a way of thinking that emphasized humans, right?
sentences.zh: 当时人们关注的是人文主义。这是一种强调人类的思维方式，对吧？

sentences.en: Emphasized human potential and creativity.
sentences.zh: 强调人类的潜能和创造力。

sentences.en: And looked at individual people and the importance of individual achievements.
sentences.zh: 并关注个体的人以及个人成就的重要性。

sentences.en: Earlier art in Europe tended to be primarily religious, looking at scenes from the Bible or painting religious figures.
sentences.zh: 欧洲早期的艺术往往主要是宗教性的，关注《圣经》中的场景或描绘宗教人物。

sentences.en: Second, during the Renaissance, there were huge advances in art and science.
sentences.zh: 其次，在文艺复兴时期，艺术和科学取得了巨大的进步。

sentences.en: Artists began to create more realistic images.
sentences.zh: 艺术家开始创作更加逼真的图像。

sentences.en: Thinkers, and philosophers, and scientists started to question some of the old ideas about the world and study the natural world through observation.
sentences.zh: 思想家、哲学家和科学家开始质疑一些关于世界的旧观念，并通过观察来研究自然世界。

sentences.en: And third, the Renaissance is famous due to the individuals who were working during this period.
sentences.zh: 第三，文艺复兴之所以闻名，是因为这个时期涌现的杰出人物。

sentences.en: People like Michelangelo, Raphael, Galileo, and of course Leonardo da Vinci.
sentences.zh: 像米开朗基罗、拉斐尔、伽利略，当然还有列奥纳多·达·芬奇。

sentences.en: These people helped to transform art and science.
sentences.zh: 这些人帮助改变了艺术和科学。

sentences.en: I think Leonardo Da Vinci, out of everything he did in his life, is obviously best known for his art.
sentences.zh: 我认为列奥纳多·达·芬奇在他一生所做的一切中，显然最以他的艺术闻名。

sentences.en: Two of his most well-known works are the Mona Lisa and the Last Supper.
sentences.zh: 他最著名的两件作品是《蒙娜丽莎》和《最后的晚餐》。

sentences.en: These paintings are described as masterpieces.
sentences.zh: 这些画作被描述为杰作。

sentences.en: Masterpieces are the greatest works of an artist’s career.
sentences.zh: 杰作是一个艺术家职业生涯中最伟大的作品。

sentences.en: The Mona Lisa has fascinated people for centuries.
sentences.zh: 《蒙娜丽莎》几个世纪以来一直让人着迷。

sentences.en: It is believed to be a painting of a merchant’s wife, and eventually ended up in the French Royal Family’s collection.
sentences.zh: 人们认为这是一位商人之妻的肖像画，最终进入了法国皇室的收藏。

sentences.en: The Mona Lisa might be the most famous artwork in history.
sentences.zh: 《蒙娜丽莎》也许是历史中最著名的艺术品。

sentences.en: It is seen by hundreds of thousands of people a year in the Louvre, which is where it is now.
sentences.zh: 它现在所在的卢浮宫每年接待成千上万的参观者。

sentences.en: The Last Supper captures a moment from the Bible.
sentences.zh: 《最后的晚餐》捕捉了《圣经》中的一个瞬间。

sentences.en: It shows the reaction of Jesus’s disciples when he tells them that one of them will betray him.
sentences.zh: 它展示了当耶稣告诉门徒他们中有人会背叛他时，门徒们的反应。

sentences.en: And it is again, one of the most famous paintings in history.
sentences.zh: 它再次成为历史上最著名的画作之一。

sentences.en: Leonardo made art slowly. Sometimes he worked extremely slowly.
sentences.zh: 列奥纳多作画速度很慢。有时他工作极其缓慢。

sentences.en: He would spend years on a single painting.
sentences.zh: 他会在一幅画上花费数年时间。

sentences.en: For example, the Mona Lisa was likely worked on for several years, and some historians believe he never considered it finished.
sentences.zh: 例如，《蒙娜丽莎》很可能历时数年创作，一些历史学家认为他从未觉得它完成过。

sentences.en: He actually carried it with him for much of his life and he took it between various different cities.
sentences.zh: 事实上，他在生命中的大部分时间里都随身带着它，并在不同的城市之间带着它辗转。

sentences.en: And eventually when he moved to France from Italy, he took the Mona Lisa with him as well.
sentences.zh: 最终当他从意大利搬到法国时，他也把《蒙娜丽莎》带了过去。

sentences.en: Before he began painting, Leonardo would create detailed sketches and studies.
sentences.zh: 在开始作画之前，列奥纳多会创作详细的草图和研究。

sentences.en: He carefully observed human faces and muscles and different expressions.
sentences.zh: 他仔细观察人脸、肌肉和不同的表情。

sentences.en: One key technique he used was Sfumato, which is a method of softly blending colors and tones so that there are no sharp lines.
sentences.zh: 他使用的关键技术之一是晕涂法（Sfumato），这是一种柔和地融合颜色和色调、使画面没有生硬线条的方法。

sentences.en: You can clearly see this in the Mona Lisa, where the transitions between the light and the shadow are so smooth that they are almost invisible.
sentences.zh: 你可以在《蒙娜丽莎》中清晰地看到这一点，其中的明暗过渡非常平滑，几乎察觉不到。

sentences.en: Leonardo also paid attention to composition.
sentences.zh: 列奥纳多还十分注重构图。

sentences.en: Composition is the arrangement of elements in a painting.
sentences.zh: 构图是指画作中各个元素的排列。

sentences.en: In the Last Supper, for instance, all of the lines in the room, in the painting, lead your eye towards the central figure of Jesus.
sentences.zh: 例如，在《最后的晚餐》中，房间里画作中的所有线条都引导着你的目光投向核心人物耶稣。

sentences.en: But, while Leonardo is best known as an artist, he was also fascinated by how the world worked.
sentences.zh: 但是，尽管列奥纳多最著名的身份是艺术家，他也对世界的运作方式充满好奇。

sentences.en: One of his main interests was anatomy, which is the study of the human body.
sentences.zh: 他的主要兴趣之一是解剖学，即对人体结构的研究。

sentences.en: To understand anatomy better, he carefully cut open human and animal bodies to study their bones and their muscles and their organs.
sentences.zh: 为了更好地理解解剖学，他仔细剖开人和动物的身体来研究它们的骨骼、肌肉和器官。

sentences.en: This was unusual at the time, but it allowed him to produce incredibly detailed and accurate drawings of the human body.
sentences.zh: 这在当时很不寻常，但这使他能够绘制出极其详细且准确的人体图纸。

sentences.en: Leonardo also designed a wide range of machines, including early ideas for flying machines and tanks and weapons.
sentences.zh: 列奥纳多还设计了各种各样的机器，包括早期对飞行器、坦克和武器的构想。

sentences.en: These were early models or concepts of inventions that had never been built before.
sentences.zh: 这些是从未被建造过的新发明的早期模型或概念。

sentences.en: For example, he sketched things that resembled helicopters and parachutes.
sentences.zh: 例如，他画了一些类似于直升机和降落伞的东西。

sentences.en: He also designed practical structures, such as bridges.
sentences.zh: 他还设计了实用结构，例如桥梁。

sentences.en: Some of these were intended to be portable for military use.
sentences.zh: 其中一些旨在方便军事使用而设计成便携式的。

sentences.en: Much of this work was recorded in his notebooks.
sentences.zh: 这方面的许多工作都被记录在他的笔记本中。

sentences.en: These were filled with sketches and diagrams and observations.
sentences.zh: 这些笔记本里填满了草图、图表和观察结果。

sentences.en: He wrote about everything. He wrote about, of course, art, but also human movement and how water flowed.
sentences.zh: 他什么都写。当然，他写艺术，但也写人类的运动以及水流的方式。

sentences.en: He filled his notebooks with observations about everything.
sentences.zh: 他在笔记本里写满了对万事万物的观察。

sentences.en: His notebooks also had something strange about them.
sentences.zh: 他的笔记本还有些奇怪的地方。

sentences.en: A lot of the writing is backwards. He had a habit of writing in mirror script, which means writing backwards.
sentences.zh: 很多字都是反着写的。他有一种用镜书习惯，也就是倒着写。

sentences.en: Can we call Leonardo da Vinci a scientist?
sentences.zh: 我们能称列奥纳多·达·芬奇为科学家吗？

sentences.en: On the one hand, no. He did not follow the scientific method.
sentences.zh: 一方面，不能。他没有遵循科学方法。

sentences.en: The scientific method is the structured process involving creating a hypothesis, doing an experiment, and then having results that can be repeated.
sentences.zh: 科学方法是一个结构化的过程，包括提出假设、做实验，然后得出可重复的结果。

sentences.en: This system wasn’t really around when Leonardo Da Vinci was doing his experiments or his observations.
sentences.zh: 当列奥纳多·达·芬奇做实验或观察时，这个系统其实并不存在。

sentences.en: But he did do a lot of experiments. He did lots of experimentation, lots of observation.
sentences.zh: 但他确实做了很多实验。他做了大量的实验，进行了大量的观察。

sentences.en: He questioned traditional ideas and he tried to understand cause and effect, which are some of the most important principles in modern science.
sentences.zh: 他质疑传统观念，并试图理解因果关系，这是现代科学中最核心的一些原则。

sentences.en: So he was ahead of his time, but he didn’t really use the tools or framework of modern science.
sentences.zh: 所以他超越了时代，但他并没有真正使用现代科学的工具或框架。

sentences.en: Actually, Leonardo’s curiosity was probably one of his weaknesses, as well as one of his strengths.
sentences.zh: 事实上，列奥纳多的好奇心可能既是他的优势，也是他的弱点之一。

sentences.en: Leonardo had a reputation for starting projects and then never finishing them.
sentences.zh: 列奥纳多素以喜欢开启项目却从不完成而闻名。

sentences.en: He would become fascinated by a new idea, move on, and not complete his previous work.
sentences.zh: 他会对一个新想法着迷，然后转移注意力，不再完成之前的工作。

sentences.en: Throughout his life, he moved between different important cities, including Florence, Milan, and eventually France.
sentences.zh: 在他的一生中，他在不同的重要城市之间辗转，包括佛罗伦萨、米兰，最后是法国。

sentences.en: These moves were often connected to work, as he relied on wealthy patrons to support him.
sentences.zh: 这些搬迁通常与工作有关，因为他依赖富有的赞助人来养活自己。

sentences.en: One of Leonardo’s most important patrons was the ruler of Milan.
sentences.zh: 列奥纳多最重要的赞助人之一是米兰统治者。

sentences.en: Leonardo worked for him as an artist and an advisor.
sentences.zh: 列奥纳多曾作为艺术家和顾问为他效力。

sentences.en: Much of Leonardo’s work came through commissions.
sentences.zh: 列奥纳多的许多工作都是通过委约完成的。

sentences.en: People paid him to paint paintings or make things.
sentences.zh: 人们付钱让他画画或制作东西。

sentences.en: He was paid for specific projects such as paintings or designs.
sentences.zh: 他因特定的项目（如绘画或设计）而获得报酬。

sentences.en: But his tendency to experiment and take a lot of time frustrated his patrons, who expected quicker results.
sentences.zh: 但他喜欢实验和耗费大量时间的倾向，让期待更快看到结果的赞助人感到沮丧。

sentences.en: It’s like if you became one of my patrons, I make an episode every Friday.
sentences.zh: 这就好比如果你成了我的赞助人，我每周制作一期节目。

sentences.en: If I stopped making episodes, you probably wouldn’t want to pay me anymore.
sentences.zh: 如果我停止制作节目，你可能就不想再付钱给我了。

sentences.en: If I stopped hosting my conversation clubs, you probably wouldn’t want to pay me anymore.
sentences.zh: 如果我停止举办对话俱乐部，你可能就不想再付钱给我了。

sentences.en: And Leonardo Da Vinci, it might take him a few years before he made the painting that you had paid him for.
sentences.zh: 而列奥纳多·达·芬奇可能需要几年时间才能画出你付过钱的画作。

sentences.en: In his later years, Leonardo accepted an invitation from Francis I of France and moved to France.
sentences.zh: 晚年时，列奥纳多接受了法国国王弗朗索瓦一世的邀请移居法国。

sentences.en: He was given a position and a residence near the Royal Court and he no longer needed to worry as much about securing commissions or financial support because he had a permanent place working for the French Royal family.
sentences.zh: 他在王室附近获得了一个职位和住所，从此不再需要为争取委约或资金支持而过多担忧，因为他在法国王室拥有了一份稳定的工作。

sentences.en: His health began to decline and he likely suffered from partial paralysis, which made it more difficult for him to continue painting.
sentences.zh: 他的健康状况开始恶化，并且很可能患上了部分瘫痪，这使他更难继续画画。

sentences.en: Instead, he focused more on organizing his notes and on his past work.
sentences.zh: 相反，他把更多精力放在整理笔记和回顾过去的工作上。

sentences.en: Leonardo da Vinci died in 1519 in France.
sentences.zh: 列奥纳多·达·芬奇于1519年在法国逝世。

sentences.en: He left behind unfinished projects and countless notebooks.
sentences.zh: 他留下了未竟的项目和无数的笔记本。

sentences.en: More than 500 years after his death, Leonardo da Vinci continues to be influential today.
sentences.zh: 在逝世五百多年后的今天，列奥纳多·达·芬奇依然具有影响力。

sentences.en: In art, his impact is undeniable. Techniques like Sfumato, his focus on realism, his attention to human emotions, changed how artists worked for centuries.
sentences.zh: 在艺术领域，他的影响力不可磨灭。诸如晕涂法之类的技法、他对现实主义的专注以及对人类情感的关注，改变了几个世纪以来艺术家的创作方式。

sentences.en: While he wasn’t a scientist in the modern sense, his methods reflected a new scientific mindset that would later become part of science and art and other parts of life.
sentences.zh: 虽然他在现代意义上算不上科学家，但他的方法反映了一种新的科学思维方式，这种思维方式后来融入了科学、艺术以及生活的其他方面。

sentences.en: He designed devices that were so ahead of their time.
sentences.zh: 他设计的装置远远超越了那个时代。

sentences.en: Most of his ideas were never built or impossible, but they were incredible and they encouraged other people to imagine new devices.
sentences.zh: 他的大部分想法从未被建造或根本不可能实现，但它们极其不可思议，并鼓励其他人去构想新的装置。

sentences.en: Leonardo is often described as a polymath.
sentences.zh: 列奥纳多常被描述为博学者。

sentences.en: A polymath is someone with expertise across many fields.
sentences.zh: 博学者是指在许多领域都具备专业知识的人。

sentences.en: He is also the perfect example of the “Renaissance Man”: a person who doesn’t limit themselves to just one area of knowledge.
sentences.zh: 他也是“文艺复兴人”的完美典范：一个不把自己局限于单一知识领域的人。

sentences.en: His work is a great example of interdisciplinary thinking.
sentences.zh: 他的工作是跨学科思维的绝佳范例。

sentences.en: Interdisciplinary thinking comes from combining ideas from different subjects to create something new.
sentences.zh: 跨学科思维源于将不同学科的想法结合起来以创造出新的东西。

sentences.en: Perhaps the main evidence of Leonardo da Vinci’s legacy is that around the world almost everyone has heard of the great painter Leonardo da Vinci.
sentences.zh: 或许列奥纳多·达·芬奇遗产的主要证明是，世界各地几乎所有人都听说过伟大的画家列奥纳多·达·芬奇。

sentences.en: Or if they haven’t heard of his name, they probably know his work the Mona Lisa.​
sentences.zh: 或者即使他们没听过他的名字，大概也知道他的作品《蒙娜丽莎》。

sentences.en: Who was Leonardo da Vinci? He was an artist, an inventor, and a thinker.
sentences.zh: 列奥纳多·达·芬奇是谁？他是一位艺术家、发明家和思想家。

sentences.en: He painted masterpieces, studied the human body, designed new machines.
sentences.zh: 他绘制了杰作，研究了人体，设计了新型机器。

sentences.en: You can see his works of art in the most famous museums and galleries in cities across the world.
sentences.zh: 你可以在世界各地城市的著名博物馆和画廊里看到他的艺术作品。

sentences.en: He was undoubtedly a genius. But what do you think?
sentences.zh: 他无疑是一个天才。但你怎么看？

sentences.en: Was Leonardo da Vinci the greatest artist in history?
sentences.zh: 列奥纳多·达·芬奇是历史上最伟大的艺术家吗？

sentences.en: Should we count him as a scienti st?what do you think?
sentences.zh: 我们应该把他算作科学家吗？你怎么看？
